steps.title: Cut and drill the 2 links (printed jig)
steps.note: Both links must come out identical: the jig makes sure of it
steps.fit: A parallelogram only stays level if both links are the same length. Never drill them by eye; always use the jig.
steps.how: 1) Cut two 60 mm pieces of 1/8″ × 1/2″ aluminium flat bar (hacksaw), file the ends. 2) Lay one in the printed link jig's slot, its end against the stop, and clamp jig + bar to a piece of wood. 3) Drill 4.0 mm (5/32″) through both guide holes: they are exactly 42 mm apart. 4) Same for the second bar. 5) Round the ends with a file and deburr the holes. Check: put two 5/32″ drill bits through both links stacked together. If the bits slide in, the links match.

steps.title: Plate: cut, drill, ballast and feet
steps.note: Use the printed tower as the drilling template
steps.how: 1) Cut the sheet to 120 × 110 mm (hacksaw or a jigsaw with a metal blade) and file the edges. 2) Set the printed tower on it, centred 72 mm from the back edge, and mark through its 4 flange holes. 3) Drill those 3.4 mm (9/64″). Drill 2 × 6.5 mm (1/4″) for the ballast bolts and 4 corner holes for the feet (or use stick-on feet). 4) Each ballast is an M6 bolt up from below through 5 washers, with a nut on top. It's about 60 g each and keeps the robot from tipping toward the arm. Deburr everything: aluminium edges are sharp.

steps.title: Melt in the 7 brass inserts
hw: M3 brass heat-set insert, 4 mm long
steps.note: Soldering iron at about 230 °C; push straight, stop flush
steps.fit: Holes are 5.0 mm in the CAD, which prints at about 4.0 on this printer: the size inserts need. An insert that drops in loose wasn't melted in; one that won't start needs the hole opened with a 4 mm bit by hand.
steps.how: Inserts give the printed parts real metal threads, so you can take the robot apart and rebuild it without stripping. Where they go: 4 in the tower flange (from below), 1 in the ear on the turret (from the link side), 2 in the coupler (from the link side). For each one: put the insert on the hole, rest the iron tip in it, let it sink under light pressure (about 5 s), stop when it's flush, then press it flat with something metal while it cools. Test each with an M3 screw.

callouts.text: M3 insert in the ear (from the link side)

steps.title: Tower onto the plate
steps.note: 4 M3 screws up through the plate into the inserts
steps.how: Tower on the plate with the cable slot toward the back (the ballast side). 4 × M3 × 6 up through the plate into the flange inserts. Snug, not hard: the inserts are in plastic.

steps.title: Turntable servo (MG90S) into the tower
steps.note: Lead out through the slot first, then the servo down onto the 2 posts
steps.how: Feed the servo lead out through the slot at the bottom of the tower first. Lower the servo in, spline up and centred, tabs on the 2 posts. 2 servo-bag screws through the tabs into the posts, from above.

steps.title: Bearing into the tower
steps.note: Press the 6807 into the top of the tower, flat and fully down
steps.fit: Press fit, outer ring. The pocket is drawn 48.0 mm so it prints about 47.0, the bearing's size (same correction as the main base). Loose: one wrap of tape round the bearing. Too tight: sand the pocket wall evenly, never one side.
steps.how: Press the bearing in evenly with a flat block (a piece of wood across it) until it sits on the ledge. Push on the outer ring only.

steps.title: Turntable horn under the turret (on the table)
steps.note: Turret upside down; horn screwed onto its underside
steps.how: Take the cross horn from the MG90S bag and cut its arms to 12 mm from the centre so it fits inside the hub. Turn the turret upside down and lay the horn in the hub recess, hub sticking out (toward the servo). Drive 4 servo-bag screws through the horn's holes 8 mm out into the turret's pilots. Drill 1/16″ through the horn hole first if a hole doesn't line up.

steps.title: Turret onto the bearing and the spline
steps.note: Hub into the bearing's inner ring AND horn onto the spline together
steps.fit: Press fit, inner ring: the hub is drawn 34.3 mm and prints at about 35.0. This fit keeps the turret down on the spline, so there is no horn centre screw here (it can't be reached under the cradle). Loose: one wrap of tape on the hub.
steps.how: Servo still at 135°. Hold the turret with the cradle at the back and the round front pointing at the can position (+Y, toward the work area). Lower it so the hub enters the bearing's inner ring as the horn meets the spline, then press down evenly until it bottoms.

steps.title: Shoulder servo (MG996R) into the cradle
steps.note: Spline first through the window from behind; tabs against the cradle's back face
steps.how: Slide the MG996R in from the back (the side away from the links), spline first through the window, until its tabs sit flat on the cradle. Spline to the link side, lead toward the turret plate. 4 × #8 through the tabs into the cradle's pilots. Drive them from behind; the top 2 continue into the ear for extra grip.

steps.title: Link A on the metal horn, horn on the shoulder
steps.note: Bolt link A to the horn on the table, then press the horn on at the right angle
steps.fit: Re-teach LIFT_DOWN (link at −11°) and LIFT_UP (+11°) in the laptop panel in step 20. The swing is about 21° of the servo.
steps.how: 1) On the table: lay link A on the aluminium horn with its pivot hole on the horn's centre. Mark two of the horn's threaded holes through the link (8 mm out, both on the same side), drill them 3.3 mm, and bolt the link on with 2 × M3 × 6. 2) Shoulder servo at 90°. Press the horn onto the spline so link A points forward and about 11° below horizontal (the nearest spline tooth; 25 teeth = 14.4° per tooth, the rest is fine-tuned in software). 3) Horn centre screw through the link's pivot hole into the spline.

steps.title: Link B on the ear
hw: M3 shoulder screw, 4 mm shoulder × 4 mm
steps.note: Shoulder screw through link B into the ear's insert; the link must swing freely
steps.fit: Running fit: link B must swing under its own weight. If it drags, the shoulder is shorter than the bar (3.2 mm) plus the washer: use a 4 mm shoulder.
steps.how: Nylon washer between link B and the ear. Shoulder screw through link B into the ear insert, tightened fully: the smooth shoulder is the bearing surface, so the link turns on it while the screw stays tight.

steps.title: Coupler onto both links
hw: M3 shoulder screw, 4 mm shoulder × 4 mm
steps.note: 2 shoulder screws from the servo side, through the links into the coupler's inserts
steps.fit: The parallelogram test: lift the coupler by hand. It should rise about 16 mm and stay upright (vertical) the whole way, with no binding. If it tilts, the links aren't equal: re-drill one with the jig.
steps.how: Hold the coupler against the outside of both links' front ends. A shoulder screw goes from the servo side through each link into the coupler's inserts, lower one first. Do this before the wrist servo: once it's in, its body blocks the screwdriver.

steps.title: Wrist servo into the coupler
steps.note: Body through the coupler's bracket from the front, 2 tab screws
steps.how: Body through the coupler's bracket from the front (the claw side), lead toward the links, 2 servo-bag screws through the tabs. It's the same bracket and position as on the carriage arm, so the claw fits unchanged.

steps.title: Gripper frame onto the wrist horn (on the table)
steps.note: Horn flat on the frame's flange, 4 screws through the flange into the horn
steps.how: On the table. Take the wrist servo's cross horn from the bag and cut its two long arms to 11 mm from the centre (flush with the frame's 28 mm flange). Lay it on the flange with the hub facing AWAY from the frame (toward the servo), long arms horizontal, centre on the flange's centre. The flange has 4 pilots on the arms (2 on the long arms ~7.7 mm out, 2 on the short arms ~6 mm out): drive 4 servo-bag screws through the horn's holes into them. A hole that doesn't line up: drill 1/16″ through the horn hole into the flange.

steps.title: Both fingers, gears meshed (on the table)
steps.note: Slide them in together between the plates, open by the same angle
steps.fit: Gear mesh: try it on. Teeth engage with a little play and no binding over the full swing. Never sand or file gear teeth. Printers rarely print teeth exactly, so the file is made to be edited: if they bind, print the looser pair (cad/print/stl/finger_variants/, gear_thin 0.18 or 0.25); if they rattle, the tighter pair (0.00). Or set gear_thin in backend/cad/model.py and run backend/cad/finger_variants.py.
steps.how: Before this step: lay the cut double-arm horn (step 12) on the left gear, hub up, centred, arms pointing front-to-back (toward the can and away from it), and drill 1/16″ pilots through its 2 holes into the gear; take the horn off again. Slide both fingers in together between the plates, both opened by the same angle, so the teeth mesh symmetrically.

steps.title: Right finger axle (on the table)
steps.note: From the top through the right finger; it must swing freely
steps.fit: Ø3.9 mm running fit. The finger must swing freely on the axle. Tight: twist a 5/32 in drill through by hand.
steps.how: #6-32 from the top through the frame and the right finger, threading into the bottom plate: it is the axle.

steps.title: Horn on the left gear, then the gripper servo (on the table)
steps.note: Horn flat on the left gear, 2 screws; then the servo's spline down into the horn hub
steps.fit: Horn trimmed to Ø12 mm, flat on the gear. Cut the SG90 round horn down to Ø12 mm (flush cutters, then sand), keeping its 2 holes 5 mm from the centre (or drill 1.5 mm through the horn using the gear's pilots as the guide). A full-size horn hits the servo post. The spline must slide into the hub without force.
steps.how: 1) The double-arm horn from the SG90 bag, both arms cut to 7 mm from the centre (14 mm long): it then turns inside the frame's 16 mm opening. 2) Turn the left finger so the horn's arms point front-to-back (toward the can) and drop it through the opening onto the gear, hub up (sideways it catches the servo post next to the opening), its 2 holes over the pilots you drilled before step 10, and drive the 2 small servo-bag screws (the shortest ones in the bag) through the horn into the gear. 3) SG90 at 20° (laptop panel). Hold the SG90 upside down over the frame so its spline points down into the horn's hub and the body lies over the 2 posts; press the spline fully in (turn the finger a little until the teeth engage). 4) 2 servo-bag screws through the SG90 tabs into the posts. Check: the fingers open and close together when you turn the servo by hand (unpowered).

callouts.text: horn screws → 2 small holes, 5 mm from centre

steps.title: Claw onto the wrist servo
steps.note: Press the wrist horn (with the whole claw on it) onto the servo spline, plates level
steps.how: Wrist servo at 0° first. Hold the whole claw (frame + horn + fingers + gripper servo) with the plates level and press the horn's hub onto the wrist servo's spline until it is fully on. No centre screw: the frame covers it, and the spline teeth carry the turning force.

steps.title: Can bumper
steps.note: Silicone or rubber, 9 × 13.5 mm, superglue to the frame
steps.how: Cut 9 x 13.5 mm from the silicone sheet (or a rubber band / inner tube).
steps.glue_text: Superglue the rubber pad to the frame where the can's side touches.

steps.title: Wire it and re-teach the lift
steps.note: Same harness and pins as PART E; only the lift angles change
steps.how: Wiring: same pins as PART E of the manual: turntable on D9 (now the MG90S), lift on D10 (now the MG996R shoulder), wrist D6, gripper D5, same buck supply. The turntable now pulls less current and the lift more, and the total stays within the supply. Recommended upgrade: a PCA9685 16-channel servo board on its own 6 V supply, controlled by the Uno over I²C (SDA/SCL, 2 wires). Servo power then never goes near the Uno. Re-teach in the laptop panel: LIFT_DOWN = link A at −11°, LIFT_UP = +11° (the can rises 15.7 mm, level). The turntable and wrist angles stay as they are.

names.wrist_horn: Cross horn (from the bag), long arms cut to 11 mm
names.gripper_horn: Double-arm horn (from the bag), arms cut to 7 mm
names.lift_crank: Single-arm horn, from the bag, last hole

screw_names.sh: M3 shoulder screw, 4 mm shoulder × 4 mm long

precise.label: PRECISE FIT
precise.text: Fits that decide whether it works: identical links, bearing press fits. Check each with the real part.

try.label: TRY-FIT
try.text: Test before you tighten: pivots must swing freely, and inserts must sit flush and take a screw.

#1 Phillips + small precision screwdriver; 2.5 mm hex key for the shoulder screws
